data.name: AlAisha
data.gender_notes: AlAisha is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, AlAisha means ‘the supportive one’, ‘the trustworthy one’. This name is derived from the Arabic root ‘A-S-H’, which denotes ‘support’, ‘assistance’, and ‘trustworthiness’. The name is mentioned in Hadiths as the name of one of Prophet Muhammad's wives, Aisha bint Abu Bakr. The name AlAisha carries the meaning “Supportive, Trustworthy” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose AlAisha usually hope their child will grow to embody supportive, trustworthy and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes unwavering support, trustworthiness, and loyalty in one's faith.
data.etymology: AlAisha belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Supportive, Trustworthy.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of AlAisha total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: الأيisha
in_arabic.meaning: المرأة الكريمة، الزوجة الرجيلة، الأبنة الصالحين
in_arabic.long_meaning: الأيisha اسمٌ من أسماء النبي محمد صلّى الله عليه وسلم، ويدل على المرأة الكريمة والزوجة الرجيلة والأبنة الصالحين، يحتوي على معنى الفاعلية والجدارة والكرم، وكان اسمها قبل الزواج سودة، وقد أصبح بعد الزواج باسمه الأشهر والأكثر استعمالا، وهو من أسماء القرآن الكريم، ويُعتبر من الأسماء التي تحمل معنى الفضائل والأخلاق، ويُستخدم للإناث فقط.

in_english.name: AlAisha
in_english.meaning: Noble woman, virtuous wife, righteous daughter, honorable lady
in_english.long_meaning: AlAisha is a name derived from the Arabic root 'al-'aysha, which means 'noble woman' or 'virtuous wife'. It is also associated with the name of the wife of the Prophet Muhammad, who was known for her piety, kindness, and wisdom. In Islamic tradition, AlAisha is considered a symbol of female excellence, and is often given to girls born into Muslim families. The name is also associated with the concept of 'al-'aysha al-mu'mina, or the virtuous woman, who is described in the Quran as being obedient to her husband, kind to her children, and charitable to the poor. In modern times, the name AlAisha has become popular in many Muslim-majority countries, and is often given to girls born into families who value traditional Islamic values.
